caveats: Housing units and households are different populations. Permanently closed and vacant units are one combined source category and do not indicate homes available to rent or buy. Tenure describes occupied housing arrangements, not title verification, mortgage debt, rents or housing affordability. Districts, sectors and national aggregates overlap. Tenure percentages use their own geographic denominators and are rounded; do not add them across geographies. The 2012 district closed/vacant counts sum to 686,510, three more than the printed national total of 686,507; both are retained. No vacancy rate is inferred from the occupied and combined closed/vacant counts.
Housing-unit counts are distinct from households. Tenure shares retain the source’s one-decimal-place rounding.
grain: One housing occupancy count or tenure share by geography, category and census year
notes: The census final report provides occupied and permanently closed or vacant housing-unit counts for every district in 2012 and 2024. Its 2024 tenure table reports shares owned by a household member, rented or leased from government or private owners, rent-free, encroached, or held under other arrangements. Tenure shares cover districts and four census sectors, plus national totals.
